chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I perform ghusl in a bathing place where urination takes place and ghusl from janabah (sexual impurity) is also performed, and so some water splashes into the vessel from the ground.
So he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.إِنَاء: Vessel/container — the water container used for ghusl
key_terms.جَنَابَة: Janabah — ritual impurity requiring ghusl, such as after sexual intercourse or seminal discharge
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm — standard jurisprudential phrase indicating permissibility
key_terms.مُغْتَسَل: Bathing place, bathroom — a designated area for washing
key_terms.يَنْزُو: Splashes/bounces up — water that rebounds from the floor into the vessel

ai.seo_question: Is the water that splashes back from the bathroom floor into a vessel during ghusl considered impure?
ai.summary: Umar ibn Yazid asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the purity of water that splashes back into a vessel from the floor of a bathroom used both for urination and ghusl from janabah. The Imam ruled that there is no problem with such water, indicating that the minimal splash-back is not considered impure. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that small amounts of water that may have contacted impurities do not automatically become impure unless the impurity is clearly established.
